She has almost none of the operational problems your typical clients have because she hasn't started seeing patients yet. This is actually a rare opportunity to position The Luxora Collective as the team that helps her build it correctly the first time instead of spending the next two years fixing expensive mistakes. fileciteturn0file0 fileciteturn0file1

# Prospect Summary

## Practice Snapshot
**Name:** Tempass Hill

**Current Stage**
- Brand new independent med spa
- California
- Currently still working full-time as an RN
- Office is open and ready to accept patients
- Sole injector
- No staff
- No existing patient base
- No revenue yet
- No marketing systems
- No CRM
- No automation
- Marketing company has only created two posts so far
- Paid ads expected to begin next week. fileciteturn0file0

---

# Her Goal

Her dream is very clear.

She wants to:

- Build a successful med spa
- Replace her RN income
- Stop trading time for money
- Outsource marketing because she doesn't have time
- Bring in quality, higher-paying patients
- Build something correctly from the beginning

This is emotional because she's trying to leave nursing.

That freedom is what she's actually buying.

---

# Her Biggest Pain Points

## 1. She has no roadmap.

She's overwhelmed by all the marketing noise online.

She specifically said once she entered aesthetics her algorithm became flooded with agencies and marketing companies.

She doesn't know who to trust.

This creates uncertainty.

---

## 2. She doesn't have time.

She works as an RN.

She cannot:

- create content
- manage leads
- learn marketing
- build systems

She's trying to do two careers at once.

---

## 3. She wants to avoid making expensive mistakes.

This is actually the biggest opportunity.

She has:

- no CRM
- no automation
- no follow-up
- no sales systems
- no memberships
- no consultation process
- no patient journey

Instead of making this sound like a weakness...

Position it as an advantage.

> "You've got something most established practices don't have anymore...a blank slate."

---

## 4. She doesn't want Groupon patients.

Arlene actually planted this seed perfectly.

She agreed she wants quality clients.

Lean into that.

---

# What NOT to Talk About

Don't spend time talking about:

- retention percentages
- consultation conversions
- existing staff
- current memberships
- patient reactivation

She literally has none of those yet.

Instead...

Talk about building them BEFORE she ever needs them.

---

# Discovery Questions I Would Add

Your current script assumes an established practice.

I'd change the discovery to this.

---

"You mentioned your goal is eventually leaving nursing.

When do you hope that's a reality?"

---

"What monthly revenue would allow you to comfortably walk away from your RN position?"

---

"How many patients per week would that require?"

---

"What concerns you the most about opening your doors?"

---

"If six months from now you're still balancing nursing and trying to build this on nights and weekends...

what does that look like for you?"

---

"If we were talking one year from today...

what would success actually look like?"

---

# Your Diagnostic Summary

I would NOT diagnose marketing.

I'd diagnose lack of infrastructure.

I'd say:

> Tempass, after hearing everything today, I actually don't think your biggest challenge is marketing.

> I think marketing is just the first thing everyone thinks about because that's what every agency sells.

> What I believe is actually happening is this.

First...

You're trying to build a business while working full-time as an RN, so your time is incredibly limited.

Second...

You don't yet have the systems that take someone from stranger to lifelong patient.

Third...

Because you're just getting started, every decision you make over the next few months is going to determine whether this becomes a thriving business...or whether you're spending the next two years fixing expensive mistakes.

And honestly...

I think that's your biggest opportunity.

Because unlike most practices we work with...

you haven't built bad habits yet.

Does that feel accurate?

---

# Tailored Three-Stage Presentation

## STAGE ONE

Don't say Revenue Leak Audit.

Say this.

> Before we spend another dollar on advertising...

I want to make sure we're building the business correctly from day one.

That means understanding your market...

who you're trying to attract...

how you position yourself...

what services will generate the highest lifetime value...

and making sure every piece of your business is built intentionally instead of guessing.

That's your blueprint.

---

## STAGE TWO

Talk about building her acquisition engine.

> Since you're still working as an RN...

the business can't depend on you manually answering every inquiry.

We're going to build the systems that respond...

follow up...

book consultations...

and nurture patients automatically.

That way you're not trying to manage marketing while working twelve-hour nursing shifts.

---

## STAGE THREE

This is where you really personalize.

> One thing I never want for you...

is to build a practice where every patient only comes once.

From day one...

we'll build your consultation process...

your treatment plans...

your memberships...

your package strategy...

your follow-up...

your referrals...

so every patient becomes more valuable over time.

You're building a business...

not just buying appointments.

---

# Her Prescription

Priority One

Build the business foundation before paid advertising scales.

---

Priority Two

Implement automation and patient journey systems so she isn't managing everything herself.

---

Priority Three

Launch with memberships, packages, consultations, and retention already built into the business.

Not later.

Now.

---

# Biggest Emotional Close

This is where I'd go off script.

I'd say:

> Tempass...

one thing you said really stood out to me.

You said your goal is to eventually leave nursing.

That's not really a marketing goal.

That's a life goal.

And I think what you're really looking for isn't another company to run Facebook ads.

You're looking for someone who's already built this business before...

someone who can help you avoid the mistakes almost every new owner makes...

so you can build something that gives you the freedom you're chasing.

That's exactly why The Luxora Collective exists.

---

# Likely Objections

### "I'm just getting started."

Response:

Exactly.

That's why this is actually the least expensive time to do it.

Most owners call us after they've already wasted tens of thousands on agencies, software, and systems they have to replace.

You're getting the opportunity to build it right before those mistakes happen.

---

### "I already have a marketing company."

Don't attack them.

Say:

That's perfectly fine.

We're actually not replacing them.

Marketing is only one piece of what we do.

If they're great at generating awareness, fantastic.

Our job is making sure every lead turns into a consultation, every consultation turns into a patient, and every patient becomes a long-term client.

Those are completely different roles.

---

### "I'm nervous about investing before I'm making money."

This is likely her biggest objection.

Tie it back to her goal:

> I completely understand. Every business owner feels that way at the beginning. The question isn't whether you're going to invest. You're already investing in your practice, your space, your training, and your marketing. The real question is whether you want to figure it out through trial and error, or build it with a proven roadmap from people who've already helped practices scale. The right systems implemented now can save years of frustration and thousands of dollars later.

This call should feel much more like mentoring a first-time med spa owner than selling an established practice. If you position yourself as the experienced guide helping her build a scalable business from day one, rather than another marketing company, you'll align perfectly with her goals and the value of The Luxora Collective.
